title: See AI observability in action with Dynatrace at AWS re:Invent 2026
summary: Join Dynatrace at AWS re:Invent 2026 in Las Vegas. See AI observability in action at booth #512 and join our sessions.
body_markdown:
AI applications and agents are changing how production systems behave. Observability helps you see how they behave, what they depend on, and where their impact reaches your environment. Join Dynatrace at AWS re:Invent 2026 to see how that visibility comes to life across development, AI, and cloud operations on AWS. We’ll be in Las Vegas November 30 through December 3.


The Dynatrace and AWS partnership continues to deepen across development, AI, and cloud operations. At re:Invent, you’ll have the chance to see the latest integrations, hear how organizations are putting them into practice, and get hands-on with the technology. Plus, we have several evening events lined up for you to hang out with our experts.


Here’s


what


to


know before you go:


## Understand AI and agents in production


As AI applications and agents move into production, knowing that they’re running isn’t enough. Teams need to understand how they behave alongside the applications, infrastructure, and services they depend on.


Dynatrace AI Observability provides that runtime view across AI applications and agents on AWS. For example, the Dynatrace integration with[Amazon Bedrock AgentCore](https://www.dynatrace.com/hub/detail/amazon-bedrock-agentcore-observability/) lets teams trace agent behavior, tool usage, dependencies, and model interactions across the workflow. Dynatrace also supports AWS Strands Agents, giving teams visibility into agent execution as part of the broader production environment.


And this isn’t limited to one agent or one stage of the lifecycle. Across the Dynatrace and AWS partnership, that production intelligence can also move into the tools where teams build and operate, from Kiro in development to AWS DevOps Agent in operations.


With Arize, that visibility extends into AI evaluation, helping teams understand not only how models and agents perform in production, but whether an agents’ responses meet expected quality and behavior.


****


**Expo Hall**


[Meet us at booth #512](https://www.dynatrace.com/aws-reinvent/#sessions) or[schedule time with an expert](https://dynatrace.jifflenow.com/external-request/awsreinvent2026/meeting-request?token=ceca80e17dca694dc3f7) to see what it means when AI becomes part of the production environment.


## Bring production truth into development


What you learn in production can also make its way back into development. With[AWS Kiro](https://www.dynatrace.com/hub/detail/kiro/) and[Bluebox by Dynatrace](https://www.dynatrace.com/hub/detail/bluebox/) , developers can bring runtime evidence into the work they’re doing before the next change reaches users. The Dynatrace integration with Kiro gives developers access to real-time, governed production data, and Dynatrace Intelligence insights without leaving Kiro.


Kiro Crew extends that idea by putting production intelligence into an agentic engineering workflow. It uses Dynatrace problems, entities, relationships, and root-cause analysis to help engineers prioritize what needs attention and start investigations with evidence already in hand, while keeping people in control of actions that affect live systems.


Instead of treating production as something developers learn about only after deployment, observability and runtime intelligence can inform how they investigate issues and evaluate changes earlier in the development lifecycle.


****


**Breakout Session**


**Shipping AI Code with Confidence Using Bluebox by Dynatrace and AWS Kiro**


Western Governors University will join Dynatrace to show how production truth can support AI-assisted development, issue detection, and evidence-backed remediation.


**Tuesday, December 1, from 1:00–2:00 PM at MGM Grand**


## Put production context to work in operations


Production evidence becomes even more valuable when AI starts participating in operational investigations. The Dynatrace integration with[AWS DevOps Agent](https://www.dynatrace.com/hub/detail/aws-devops-agent/) combines Dynatrace root-cause analysis and real-time production context with AWS frontier-agent capabilities. Teams can bring Dynatrace topology and telemetry into an AI-assisted investigation rather than reconstructing the incident across separate tools. This integration is already delivering measurable results: joint customers have reported up to a[70% reduction in mean time to resolution (MTTR)](https://www.dynatrace.com/news/blog/orchestrate-multicloud-ai-agents-for-autonomous-incident-resolution/) .


This is where the move toward increasingly autonomous operations becomes tangible. The goal isn’t AI acting without visibility into the production environment. It’s giving AI-assisted operations the evidence they need to understand what happened while teams retain control over what happens next.


****


**Breakout Session**


From AI-Assisted Engineering to Autonomous Operations
